summary: A toggle for an on/off setting that takes effect as soon as it is flipped. It is a form control: it submits a value while on, resets with its form, is disabled by a disabled fieldset and validates required.

selected.note: On or off. The initial value is the state a form reset returns to. Named selected by the API vocabulary (checked is its alias).

value.note: What the control submits under its name while it is on. While off it submits nothing.

name.note: The name the value is submitted under.

label.note: The visible text and the accessible name. A switch without one warns.

description.note: A hint under the label, read together with the control.

errorMessage.note: Why the value is not accepted. Shown, and read with the control, only while validation is error.

validation.note: Set by the author. error shows the error look and message and marks the control invalid to assistive technology.

required.note: The switch must be on for the form to validate; while off it is invalid (value missing).

disabled.note: Unavailable: cannot be focused or toggled and submits nothing. A disabled fieldset ancestor has the same effect without changing this property.

anatomy.name: root
anatomy.notes: The whole switch: control and text column side by side.

anatomy.name: control
anatomy.notes: The focusable on/off control the person operates.

anatomy.name: track
anatomy.notes: The pill the thumb slides in; its fill shows on or off.

anatomy.name: thumb
anatomy.notes: The knob; sits at the start while off and at the end while on.

anatomy.name: content
anatomy.notes: One column holding the label, description and error message beside the control.

anatomy.name: label
anatomy.notes: Visible name, with a required mark when required.

anatomy.name: error
anatomy.notes: Shown only while validation is error.

label.notes: The visible text and accessible name, given by the label prop.

change.note: Fires when the person flips the switch, after selected has its new value. Not fired for a programmatic change or a form reset.

hover.trigger: Pointer over the control or its label.
hover.note: No separate look; the pointer cursor shows the control is operable.

active.trigger: Pointer or Space held down on the control.

disabled.trigger: disabled is true, or a disabled fieldset ancestor.

accessibility.native: An <input type=checkbox role=switch>: it supplies focus, Space activation, the on/off state and form participation.
accessibility.accessibleNameSource: The label prop. A <label for> pointing at the switch activates it but does not name it.

formAssociation.note: Form-associated through the shared mixin. Submits value under name only while selected; form.reset() restores the initial selected state; a disabled fieldset disables it and re-enabling restores it; required makes it invalid while off (value missing) and reportValidity() focuses the control; <label for> toggles it.

accessibility.targetSize: The clickable area (control plus label) is at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels in both sizes. PROPOSAL: the small control is padded to 24px high because its track is 16px.
accessibility.focusRingVisible: A ring appears on keyboard focus only, at least 3:1 against the background, outside the track so it is not clipped.
accessibility.missingNameWarning: A one-time console warning when label is empty.

keyboard.Tab: Moves focus to or from the switch. A disabled switch is skipped.
keyboard.Enter: Does not flip the switch; submits the owning form, as a native checkbox does.

aria: role=switch with aria-checked following selected (supplied by the native checkbox).
aria-describedby lists the description and, only while validation is error, the error message.
announcements: Name, role switch and state on or off on focus.
The new state on or off after each flip.
The description, and the error while invalid, read after the name.

useCases.when: A setting that applies immediately when flipped (notifications, dark mode, airplane mode).
useCases.use: sb-switch with a label, and a description when the effect needs explaining.

useCases.when: A boolean field in a form that is submitted with the form.
useCases.use: sb-switch with name and value; add required when it must be on.

useCases.when: A compact control in a dense list or table row.

useCases.use: sb-switch with validation=error and an errorMessage.

antiPatterns.pattern: A switch for a choice that only takes effect after the form is submitted, such as agreeing to terms.
antiPatterns.why: A switch implies the change is immediate; a deferred choice reads as a checkbox.
The control has no accessible name and warns at runtime.
antiPatterns.alternative: Always set label; there is no label-less variant.

antiPatterns.pattern: Two or more switches standing in for one choice among several options.
antiPatterns.why: Switches are independent; they do not express exclusivity.

openQuestions.question: Name the on/off prop selected (the API vocabulary) or checked (the native name)?
openQuestions.recommendation: selected: checked is registered as its alias, and check A1 rejects an unregistered spelling.
openQuestions.answer: selected. The inner native input still uses checked internally.

openQuestions.question: Does the component set validation=error itself when required is unmet?
openQuestions.recommendation: No: validation stays author-set, and the browser's own :invalid and reportValidity() cover the required state. The component cannot know when to start showing errors (touched, submitted) as well as the form can.
openQuestions.answer: No. Authors set validation=error and errorMessage; required still blocks submission natively.

openQuestions.question: Should Enter flip the switch?
openQuestions.recommendation: No: Space flips it as the APG switch pattern requires, and Enter submits the form like a native checkbox.
openQuestions.answer: Enter submits the owning form and does not flip.

openQuestions.question: What does the default value submit while on?
Which two sizes?
openQuestions.recommendation: small and medium (default medium), the two steps the API size vocabulary names for a compact and a regular control; the existing semantic size.switch tokens already give both.
openQuestions.answer: small and medium; no tiny or large.

openQuestions.question: How is the error message tied to the control for assistive technology?
openQuestions.recommendation: Add its id to aria-describedby while validation is error, plus aria-invalid. aria-errormessage has weaker support. The shared native-control mixin builds describedBy from the description only, so the implementation extends it for the error id.

openQuestions.question: A read-only mode, and a hidden-label mode?
openQuestions.recommendation: Neither: not requested, and a read-only switch has no native equivalent. Add them when a use case appears.
